title: KEMIS registration checklist for Kenyan schools
description: A practical checklist for registering learners on KEMIS: the data to gather, the mistakes that cause problems, and how to record UPI numbers once assigned.
body:
KEMIS, the Kenya Education Management Information System, took over from NEMIS in January 2026, and schools register their learners on it directly through the government portal. Registration only goes as smoothly as the records behind it. Most delays trace back to the same few problems: missing fields, names that do not match the birth certificate, and the wrong certificate number.

This checklist covers what to prepare before you sit down at the portal. It draws on published guides to KEMIS registration, and the Ministry's requirements can change, so confirm the details for your school level with your county or sub-county education office.

Before you start

Published guides report three things about the school itself:

  • Schools register on KEMIS afresh, rather than carrying their NEMIS registration over.
  • Learner registration begins only after the institution's own registration has been approved, reportedly by the county or sub-county education office.
  • Registration is described as mandatory for public and private schools alike.

The learner data to gather

Requirements vary by level, for example KJSEA details apply to secondary learners. The guides list these items for each learner:

  • Full name (first, middle and last), exactly as it appears on the birth certificate.
  • Date of birth, matching the certificate.
  • Sex.
  • The birth certificate entry number.
  • Admission number and current grade or class.
  • Nationality, and county, sub-county and location of birth.
  • Parent or guardian names and identification details.
  • Previous school details.
  • KJSEA index number or year, for secondary learners.
  • Medical condition, disability or special needs, where they apply.
  • A photograph, and copies of the birth certificate and parent or guardian ID, which some guides say schools must upload.

The mistakes that cause trouble

Entering the wrong certificate number

Guidance on KEMIS asks for the official birth certificate entry number, not the printed serial number. One parent registration form describes the entry number as the one shown above the date of birth. Check the certificate itself before you copy a number into your records.

Names that do not match the certificate

Names are expected to match the birth certificate strictly. Nicknames, swapped first and middle names, initials and spelling variations are the usual causes of mismatches.

Learners without a birth certificate

Published guides say a school may use a Birth Not Yet Registered (BNYR) number or, in special cases, an affidavit, as a temporary measure while the certificate is obtained. The birth certificate is described as mandatory for primary learners. Follow your education office's guidance on each case.

Blank dates of birth and gender

These are simple gaps that stop a registration. They are also the easiest to find early, if you look for them before registration day.

Duplicates and wrong classes

A learner entered twice, or left in last year's class after promotion, creates corrections you would rather not make on the portal.

Do the checking first: Finding forty learners with missing certificate details is far easier before registration starts than in the middle of it. Run a completeness check on your records before anyone logs in.

A step-by-step plan

  1. List the gaps. Find every learner missing a date of birth, gender or birth certificate number.
  2. Collect the missing details. Ask parents to confirm their child's information. Some schools have used a KEMIS learner registration form for this, which asks parents to certify that the details are accurate.
  3. Correct your records. Make names, dates and certificate numbers match the documents.
  4. Put every field in one place. Prepare a worksheet of the fields KEMIS asks for, so you can copy values into the portal instead of re-typing.
  5. Register in batches. Work class by class, and note any errors as you go.
  6. Record each UPI. Keep a two-column list of admission number and UPI as numbers are assigned.
  7. Check the result. Confirm that every enrolled learner has a UPI on file.

Recording UPI numbers

According to published guides, KEMIS generates a learner's UPI when the learner is registered or an existing record is updated. Some guides call the number a ULI instead, so use whichever label the portal shows. Load the numbers back into your school's records, so that report cards, exam entries and reports all use the same identifier for each learner.

Where Edupath helps

KEMIS does not currently offer a public developer API, so registration itself still happens on the government portal. Edupath's KEMIS Readiness tools cover the preparation on either side of it:

  • A bulk import for UPI numbers, from a two-column CSV of admission numbers and UPI numbers.
